RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 3

Both you and the appointed candidate are men, so the panel's composition can't plausibly explain your rejection. An all-male panel is a legitimate concern about institutional process in general, but raising it here would look like grasping — and it would weaken the part of your case that is genuinely strong.

That part is simple: on paper you out-qualify him (completed PhD, six papers, four years teaching vs. unfinished PhD, two papers), and the university has ignored a reasonable request for written reasons. Most public universities have a legal or policy duty to provide them.

Send a dated follow-up, cite the relevant policy, copy HR, and ask about the appeals deadline. Keep it procedural.
